aboutGame.title: What is Transport Fever 3?
paragraphs: Transport Fever 3 is a transport tycoon simulation from Urban Games where you build and manage rail, road, sea and air networks across more than 120 years of transport history. Plan freight supply chains, connect cities and industries, and grow a company from a single depot into a continent-spanning logistics empire.

The game ships with 300+ vehicles, procedurally generated maps and climate zones, story campaigns, sandbox and multiplayer modes, plus a built-in mod browser and map editor. Our wiki covers every system with beginner guides, vehicle lists, industry chains, station design and proven network strategies.

modules.name: Transport Fever 3 Beginner Guide
modules.description: Get your first profitable network running with core mechanics, freight routes, finances and signaling explained step by step.

highlights.detail: Plan before you spend — pause the game and study the contour and land-use overlays before laying track.
Start with freight — short, linear road or rail chains earn steady income before passenger lines.
Keep chains simple — move raw materials to a processing plant, then finished goods into a city.
Protect cash flow — hold reserves or reinvest in high-yield freight instead of repaying your loan early.

modules.name: Transport Fever 3 Vehicles
modules.description: Compare trains, trams, buses, trucks, ships, aircraft and helicopters by capacity, cost and the routes they serve best.

highlights.label: Rail
highlights.detail: High-capacity locomotives and wagons for bulk freight and intercity passenger corridors.

highlights.label: Road
highlights.detail: Flexible trucks and buses handle first-mile collection and last-mile city distribution.

highlights.label: Maritime
highlights.detail: Ships and barges move heavy bulk cargo and bridge island gaps at a low unit cost.

highlights.label: Aviation
highlights.detail: Aircraft deliver fast long-distance passengers and high-value cargo over rough terrain.

modules.name: Transport Fever 3 Transport Guide
modules.description: Design road, rail, sea and air networks that stay efficient as traffic grows, from signal spacing to modular station hubs.

highlights.detail: Dual one-way track — build dedicated up and down lines on mainline corridors to avoid deadlocks.
Signal spacing — place block signals roughly 1.5 train lengths apart on straight track.
Clean junctions — keep crossings clear and separate freight flows from passenger traffic.
Modular hubs — dedicate platforms to express, commuter and freight services, with grade-separated flyovers.

modules.name: Transport Fever 3 Industry Guide
modules.description: Follow raw materials through processing and manufacturing to keep every factory shipping and every city supplied.

highlights.label: Tier 1
highlights.detail: Extraction — logs, iron ore, coal, crude oil, grain and stone feed the whole supply chain.

highlights.label: Tier 2
highlights.detail: Processing — mills, refineries and plants convert raw inputs into planks, steel and refined oil.

highlights.label: Tier 3
highlights.detail: Manufacturing — advanced plants build tools, machines, goods, fuel and food for city districts.
A steel mill consumes two iron ore and two coal to yield one unit of steel.
Keep shipping above 70–80% of output to trigger factory upgrades instead of downgrades.

modules.name: Transport Fever 3 Maps
modules.description: Choose the right map size, climate zone and terrain for your network, from compact commuter maps to transcontinental layouts.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: Megalomaniac (1:4–1:5) — 35+ towns for transcontinental express runs and massive classification yards.

highlights.label: A
highlights.detail: Large (1:2–1:3) — 20–30 towns ideal for multi-tiered passenger rail and freight terminals.

highlights.label: B
highlights.detail: Medium (1:1–1:2) — 12–18 towns, perfect for regional hubs and interconnected freight loops.

highlights.label: C
highlights.detail: Small (1:1) — 6–10 towns, best for local bus routes and short-haul commuter trains.

modules.name: Transport Fever 3 Campaign
modules.description: Work through every historical era, mission objective and bonus task in the story-driven Transport Fever 3 campaign.

highlights.label: Pioneers
highlights.detail: Era 1 (1850–1900) — steam locomotives and wagons hug contours to beat steep terrain.

highlights.label: Industry
highlights.detail: Era 2 (1900–1950) — heavy freight rail and trams serve dense manufacturing webs.

highlights.label: Modern
highlights.detail: Era 3 (1950+) — electrified mainlines, air cargo hubs and high-speed passenger rail.

highlights.label: Bonus
highlights.detail: Optional milestones and bonus tasks reward efficient, well-balanced transport networks.

modules.name: Transport Fever 3 Tips and Tricks
modules.description: Fast, practical advice on signals, cash flow, hub design and data overlays to keep your transport empire running smoothly.

highlights.label: Signals
highlights.detail: Space block signals at 1.5 train lengths and keep junction fouling points clear.

highlights.label: Cash Flow
highlights.detail: Avoid deadheading, match fleet size to supply and reinvest in high-yield freight.

highlights.label: Hubs
highlights.detail: Separate freight, commuter and express platforms, and use flyovers at busy junctions.

highlights.label: Overlays
highlights.detail: Use contour, land-use and cargo-flow layers to diagnose bottlenecks before you build.

faq.title: Transport Fever 3 FAQ
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about Transport Fever 3.

items.question: What is Transport Fever 3?
items.answer: Transport Fever 3 is a transport tycoon simulation from Urban Games. You build rail, road, sea and air networks, manage freight supply chains and grow a transport company across 120+ years of history. It released on September 29, 2026 for PC, PS5 and Xbox.

items.question: Is Transport Fever 3 beginner friendly?
items.answer: Yes. Start with short freight routes such as grain or oil, keep supply chains simple and study the contour and land-use overlays before spending money on track. Our Transport Fever 3 beginner guide walks through your first profitable line.

items.question: How do I make money fast in Transport Fever 3?
items.answer: Prioritize short, high-demand freight chains with fast turnaround times, avoid empty return trips and match fleet capacity to factory output. Reinvesting in high-yield freight lines beats paying off your starting loan early.

items.question: What platforms is Transport Fever 3 available on?
items.answer: Transport Fever 3 is available on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox, and it supports cross-platform mod sharing through the in-game mod browser and Steam Workshop.

items.question: Does Transport Fever 3 support mods?
items.answer: Yes. Transport Fever 3 includes a built-in mod browser and map editor, with community vehicle packs, station assets, economic rebalances and scripting tools expanding the base game.

items.question: How many vehicles are in Transport Fever 3?
items.answer: Transport Fever 3 features more than 300 vehicles spanning trains, trams, buses, trucks, ships, aircraft and helicopters across its historical eras.
